title: Risk review of the proposed discovery redesign

requirements.DRR01: Challenge the proposed architecture for correctness and scalability gaps.
requirements.DRR02: Check existing client and backend contracts before recommending changes.
requirements.DRR03: Identify required design decisions and validation without changing runtime behavior.

verdict: Proceed with the direction, but do not implement the proposal unchanged. Versioned ordering, selective filtering and uniform Random still require concrete designs and bounded resource accounting.

risks.risk: A cursor does not freeze mutable ordering or membership.
risks.evidence: An in-memory example returns A and B, then after score changes returns D and A; A repeats and C is skipped. Current tests also require previously selected version IDs to survive rating changes, new publications and API restart.
risks.mitigation: Specify what remains frozen: sort keys, logical membership, version IDs and mutable filter values. Current restrictions/redaction must override history. Prototype retained versioned rows/chunks and expiry; never hold a database transaction open for a browsing session.

risks.risk: Shared ranking generations can relocate whole-catalogue copying into a worker.
risks.evidence: Illustrative naive design: 10 million tracks * 4 feeds * 30 one-minute generations = 1.2 billion retained ranking rows; full copying writes about 666667 rows/second.
risks.mitigation: Budget generation construction, retained versions, bytes and cleanup. Share unchanged data or use versioned changes where practical. Explicitly account for algorithm changes that affect every track. Core PostgreSQL materialized-view refresh reexecutes the query; it is not automatic incremental maintenance.

risks.risk: LIMIT and keyset paging do not bound arbitrary filter work.
risks.evidence: Rare substring/rating/biome combinations and large personal exclusions can force many examined candidates. A trigram pattern without extractable trigrams can scan the index.
risks.mitigation: Define supported query classes and indexes, total database/request deadlines, candidate budgets and admission costs. Distinguish budget exhaustion from an exhausted result set. Cursor progress must consume rejected candidates without losing unreturned lookahead rows. Preserve existing short-search semantics unless an explicit contract change is chosen.

risks.risk: Uniform Random cannot guarantee a result within a fixed generic rejection budget for all selective filters.
risks.evidence: With eligible fraction 1 in 1000000 and 1000 independent uniform trials, success probability is about 0.09995%. Current tests require finding the sole still-visible track and allow the current track when it is the only eligible one.
risks.mitigation: Specify sampling population and exact uniformity, exclusion fallback, supported pools, retry/exhaustion response and membership freshness. Avoid nearest-UUID sampling bias and truncated top-N pools. Test distribution and sparse eligibility, not just one successful pick.

risks.risk: Asynchronous projection can miss, duplicate or reorder source changes.
risks.evidence: Publication, new revisions, rating changes, profile names, restrictions, artificial classification, redaction and expiry all affect discovery, through multiple existing writers.
risks.mitigation: Use a durable transactional change journal/outbox, monotonic source revisions and idempotent consumers; define ordering ownership. Coalesce writes outside competitive transactions, monitor lag and run bounded reconciliation. Backfills must not overwrite newer live changes.

risks.risk: Last-finish popularity expiry can decrement a refreshed contribution.
risks.evidence: A pair last seen on day 0 has expiry day 7. A new finish on day 6 refreshes it to day 13. The old day-7 expiry must not remove the day-6 contribution.
risks.mitigation: Use event-time max updates and version-checked expiration, explicit watermark semantics and idempotent increment/decrement. Cover late/duplicate events, retries, rule/car/version deduplication, creator-proof/test-driver exclusion, account restrictions and recovery. Do not sum daily distinct counts as an exact seven-day distinct count.

risks.risk: Per-track counters and expiry scheduling can become new write hot spots.
risks.evidence: A very popular track receives concentrated finishes. The earlier illustrative 20 million races/day permits up to 140 million distinct track/player pairs across seven days before deduplication.
risks.mitigation: Partition event ingestion/projection, batch or coalesce track updates and bound expiry work. Measure state size, index/WAL write amplification, vacuum and retention. Do not add a globally locked generation counter or new expensive work to accepted-race finalization.

risks.risk: Projection or shared cache lag can expose stale identities or restricted tracks.
risks.mitigation: Maintain current authoritative visibility checks at page/detail/document/race boundaries. Keep cached candidate ordering separate from current delivery eligibility. Handle hide, deletion, redaction, block/unblock and re-enable while old cursors are active. Cache keys and cursors must bind endpoint/query version, filters, account/personal scope and expiry; rotation and multiple replicas must be handled.

risks.risk: Removing totals/offsets changes the browser's interaction model.
risks.evidence: The gallery sizes its horizontal extent from the exact total. It uses discovery_index to position selections and Random, and loads evicted pages by absolute position.
risks.mitigation: Design windowed gallery coordinates, bidirectional cursors, cursor checkpoints and bounded eviction together. Preserve fast swipes, back from details/racing, selected-track focus, acknowledged-publication pinning, offline first-page caching, expiry and account changes. A direct selected-ID fetch opens the card but does not itself locate its surrounding filtered page.

risks.risk: Personal history remains a large per-request input and destroys shared-cache reuse.
risks.evidence: Current requests can carry up to 50000 favorite or raced IDs. These are locally supplied history semantics, not necessarily verified account history.
risks.mitigation: Keep membership checks indexed or use bounded account/session-scoped collection references where consistent with the contract. Avoid resending and sorting large lists for every page. Do not silently substitute server-verified races or cross-device collections for device-local history.

risks.risk: Recommendation mixing, search ties and score representation can alter behavior or cursor order.
risks.mitigation: Retain three-official/one-community mixing with two cursors and a phase; define exhaustion and filtering behavior and ensure unrated community tracks remain reachable. Include every sort key and a unique ID, with correct mixed directions, null handling, deterministic score precision and collation/algorithm versioning. Keep selected published revisions and old direct links intact.

risks.risk: Migration and compatibility can preserve the expensive path indefinitely.
risks.mitigation: Capture changes before snapshot/backfill, validate by source watermark, shadow-compare bounded queries and canary the new API/client contract. Version disk caches and handle old cursors. Define a bounded old-client support period and safe rollback. Avoid falling back to full catalogue rebuilding during overload. Budget concurrent index creation, backfill disk/WAL and worker/database capacity.

risks.risk: Validating page latency alone can hide worker, database and completeness failures.
risks.mitigation: Measure rows examined, SQL plans/buffers, scheduled p95/p99, queue age, projection freshness, writes/WAL, peak memory and cleanup under skew. Test missing/duplicate logical tracks, page expiry, late events, sparse Random, worker failure/replay, profile mass updates and artificial/human eligibility. Account count, track count, revision count, recent pair count and query selectivity are independent dimensions.

required_design_decisions: Exact snapshot guarantees for order, filter membership and selected published version versus current visibility.
Concrete retained-ranking storage, update cadence, cursor lifetime and peak byte/write budgets.
Uniform Random supported-query policy and behavior when a bounded search cannot establish a result.
Client browsing/selection model after removing exact totals and arbitrary offsets.
Projection freshness and recovery guarantees, with authority for every input field.
Old-client coexistence, rollout and rollback boundaries.
recommended_next_step: Design and measure a narrow indexed New-feed prototype plus its versioned client paging/selection behavior. In parallel on paper, specify ranking-history storage and Random contracts. Do not generalize all feeds and filter combinations until these unresolved costs are demonstrated.

validation.checks: Read current discovery implementation, client paging/gallery and existing discovery tests; read official PostgreSQL documentation; run an in-memory Python cursor-mutation, rejection-probability and naive-generation-size example. No production query or capacity benchmark.

mutable_score_example.consequence: A repeats and C is missed

validation.limitation: These are plan risks and source-contract findings, not measurements of a proposed implementation. Existing tests were inspected rather than rerun; no runtime code changed.
